llm.summary: This ClawHub skill is documentation-only and its requirements/instructions are consistent with its stated purpose — the real runtime risk comes from the separate npm package it instructs you to install.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description match its behavior: it is documentation and installer guidance for the real MoltGuard npm plugin. It requests no credentials, no binaries, and has no install spec, which is appropriate for a docs-only skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tells the agent how to verify and install the npm package (npm view, npm pack, openclaw plugins install) and documents expected file paths/network endpoints that belong to the npm package. The instructions do not themselves access user secrets or system files, but they explicitly guide installing software that will.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or code is bundled with the skill (instruction-only). The skill points to an npm package on the public registry — this is a reasonable, low-risk installation pattern for a plugin installer skill.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. It documents that the npm package will store credentials under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/, which is reasonable for a plugin that manages agent protections.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and default agent invocation settings are appropriate. The skill itself does not request persistent privileges or modify other skills' configs; however installing the npm plugin will add persistent behavior (local gateway, hooks) — the SKILL.md calls this out.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This ClawHub skill is documentation-only and appears coherent. The real security decision is whether to install and trust the npm package @openguardrails/moltguard. Before installing: verify the package provenance (npm view repository.url), download and inspect the tarball (npm pack && tar -xzf), compare with the GitHub repo, review critical files (entry points, network client, sanitizer), install and run in an isolated sandbox first, monitor network traffic (mitmproxy/tcpdump/Little Snitch), and check the credentials directory (~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/) and any created local gateway ports. If you do not want the agent to perform the install automatically, run the install manually and avoid allowing autonomous agent actions until you've audited the package.
